entries.eco: ECO-10. FEEDFORWARD caps across the top leg of each divider (VOUT -> FB, verified from the netlist), so the zero they set is 1/(2*pi*R_top*C). Dropping R_top 10x without touching C would move it from ~6 kHz to ~60 kHz and discard the phase lead it exists to provide, so 15 pF -> 150 pF holds it where the design put it. The datasheet says only that 'a typical value of 15pF will generally suffice', so this preserves MouseBiteLabs' compensation rather than following a mandate. C0G +/-1% 100 V AEC-Q200 -- a compensation element should not drift with temperature.

entries.note: SWAPPED 2026-08-19 from GRM188R61E106KA73J, which was at ZERO stock at both distributors with a 17-week lead (verified 2026-08-19). BOM-only: the board Value stays `10u` and no board file changes, so unlike ECO-8's Value edits this one cannot be reverted by a PCB-from-schematic sync -- but the SCHEMATIC's own Source link for these seven still points at the GRM, so update it there too before anyone regenerates a BOM from the schematic. Verified parameter-by-parameter against the incumbent on the Digi-Key API: capacitance 10 uF, rated voltage 25 V, dielectric X5R, package 0603 (1608), max thickness 1.00 mm and operating range -55 to +85 C are ALL IDENTICAL. Two differences, both neutral-or-better here: tolerance loosens from +/-10% to +/-20%, which is immaterial on bulk decoupling and is dwarfed by MLCC DC-bias derating anyway; and the GRT is Murata's soft-termination series and is AEC-Q200 automotive-qualified, which the GRM is not. WHY THE VOLTAGE MATTERED MORE THAN THE TOLERANCE: the seven placements sit on VOUT3 (3.228 V), VCC (<=3.2 V), VAUD (2.5 V), VDD2 (2.5 V), U17-VDD and /D1A, and the power review flagged DC-bias derating as the thing to protect. Rated voltage drives derating far harder than the tolerance band does, so holding 25 V and giving up the tolerance grade is the right way round.
entries.alternate: GRT188R61C106KE13D if you want DEPTH and a SECOND SOURCE more than you want the 25 V rating: 10 uF +/-10% 16 V X5R 0603, Digi-Key 764,592 and Mouser 456,339 (verified 2026-08-19), versus the fitted GRT part's 192,299 at Digi-Key and ZERO at Mouser. It also restores the incumbent's +/-10% tolerance. The cost is the one thing this swap was chosen to protect: 16 V instead of 25 V in the same 0603 case means noticeably more capacitance lost to DC bias. Breakdown is not the issue -- the highest of these seven rails is 3.23 V, so 16 V is still 5x headroom.
entries.desc: 10 µF ±20% 25V Ceramic Capacitor X5R 0603 (1608 Metric)

entries.note:
SWAPPED 2026-08-19 from GRM21BR61E226ME44L, which was at ZERO stock at both distributors with a 17-week lead (verified 2026-08-19). This is the SAME GRM->GRT move made on the 10 uF line, and for the same reason. Verified parameter-by-parameter on the Digi-Key API against the incumbent: capacitance 22 uF, tolerance +/-20%, RATED VOLTAGE 25 V, dielectric X5R, package 0805 (2012 Metric), max thickness 1.45 mm and operating range -55 to +85 C are ALL IDENTICAL. The only difference is that the GRT is Murata's soft-termination series and is AEC-Q200 automotive-qualified, which the GRM is not. Nothing is given up. 2,022 in stock at Digi-Key (verified 2026-08-19) = 674 boards' worth at 3 per board; Mouser has none, so this line is single-sourced. BOM-only: board Value stays `22u`, no board file moves -- but the SCHEMATIC's Source link for these three still points at the GRM and needs the same edit.
CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ENTRY IN THIS FILE: it previously said 'NO LIKE-FOR-LIKE EXISTS -- every 22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 from a tier-1 maker is at zero', and recommended dropping to a 16 V part. THAT WAS WRONG. It came from a keyword search that filtered on stock >= 5,000, which silently excluded every real 25 V candidate -- all of which sit in the hundreds-to-thousands. A threshold chosen to shorten a search result had turned into a claim about the market. The deep sweep that found this one scanned 1,297 results across 15 query shapes with no stock floor.
entries.alternate:
GRM21BC81E226ME44K if you want depth: Murata, 25 V, 0805, +/-20%, same 1.45 mm max thickness, 7,338 in stock at Digi-Key (verified 2026-08-19) -- 3.6x the fitted part -- and a WIDER temperature range, -55 to +105 C against the X5R's -55 to +85 C. The catch is that it is X6S, a DIFFERENT DIELECTRIC FORMULATION, and DC-bias behaviour is exactly what holding 25 V was meant to protect. I could NOT verify its bias curve against the X5R's: Murata publishes that data only through SimSurfing, whose API returns HTTP 500 from here, and the product PDFs do not carry the curve. So the conservative pick is the part that changes nothing. If you have SimSurfing access, compare the two at 5 V bias and take the better one -- the extra stock is real.
Also checked and REJECTED: ZRA21CR61E226ME01L (Murata, 25 V X5R, 5,330 in stock) looks ideal in a Mouser listing but Digi-Key's parameters give its package as 'Nonstandard SMD' at 1.65 mm thick, not 0805/1.45 mm. It is not a drop-in. KGM21AR51E226MU (Kyocera AVX, 25 V X5R 0805, 612 at Digi-Key + 5 at Mouser, $1.06, 28-week lead) is a genuine second source if both Murata parts dry up.
The 16 V option remains available and is NO LONGER RECOMMENDED, since 25 V is in stock: GRM21BR61C226ME44L, 95,529 at Digi-Key. It costs DC-bias capacitance on C21's 5 V rail, which the component review flagged as mattering. Take it only if every 25 V part above is gone.

entries.eco: ECO-10. The LTC3527 specifies FB input current as 1 nA typ / 50 nA MAX. With the original 1.69M/1.00M and 1.78M/560k dividers that worst case moves VOUT3 by +/-85 mV (+/-2.62%) and VOUT5 by +/-89 mV (+/-1.77%) -- more than the resistors' own tolerance, and more than the 108 mV ECO-8 trimmed off VOUT3 to save 6.1 mW. Scaling both dividers 10x down keeps the ratio and therefore the rail, cuts the bias error to +/-8.4 / +/-8.9 mV, and lands on values where 0.1% +/-25ppm thin film exists -- which it does not at 1.69M or 1.78M, because nobody builds precision resistors that high for exactly this reason. Costs 0.13 mW of extra divider current. All four legs are YAGEO RT0603 so both dividers track on ONE film system. R55 = VOUT3 bottom leg, was 1M.
